fatal_errors: The proposed coherent L12 precipitates are crystallographically inconsistent with the stated BCC matrix unless a separate FCC-derived phase forms; Al additions to refractory BCC alloys more commonly promote B2 or other intermetallic ordering.
No prior-study evidence or citations support L12 precipitation, the proposed aging window, creep improvement, density benefit, or preservation of room-temperature properties.
The intervention, alloy system, structural mediator, test regime, mechanism, and outcomes do not reconstruct the Cr-modified HfMoTaTiZr target.
The baseline omits controlled aging, so the experiment can confound the effects of Al addition and heat treatment.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses turbine-relevant high-temperature capability, density, and room-temperature retention, and it proposes a reasonably direct microscopy-plus-mechanical-testing falsification experiment. However, it is not aligned with the target intervention of 4.2 at.% Cr in HfMoTaTiZr, the reticulated approximately 4 vol.% Laves phase, or the measured room-temperature strength–ductility improvement. More importantly, its central L12-in-BCC precipitation premise is scientifically doubtful without evidence for formation of an FCC-derived coherent phase. The expected creep benefit and room-temperature preservation are qualitative and lack effect sizes, fixed loads, density predictions, or cited support. A factorial comparison of unaged and aged alloys with and without Al would also be needed to isolate alloying from heat-treatment effects.
